description: Execute a bounded, read-only JavaScript Code Mode snippet against fallow's MCP host API. `code` must be a JavaScript function expression or function body that receives `{ fallow, root }` and returns a JSON-serializable value. The embedded sandbox exposes only a typed `fallow` object with read-only analysis calls: analyze, combined, checkChanged, checkArchitecture, securityCandidates, findDupes, projectInfo, traceExport, traceFile, impactClosure, traceDependency, traceClone, checkHealth, audit, explain, listBoundaries, featureFlags, impact, checkRuntimeCoverage, getHotPaths, getBlastRadius, getImportance, getCleanupCandidates, plus `fallow.run(tool, params)` for the same allowlist. Similar-code (15-minute timeouts) and mutation are excluded; use the standalone find_similar_code, inspect_similar_code, mutation_plan, and mutation_inspect MCP tools. Mutating fix tools are intentionally not exposed. The sandbox has no filesystem, network, module imports, process, require, Deno, Bun, or shell access, and no dynamic code compilation: eval, Function, and the async and generator function constructors are removed, including the `constructor` route reachable through function prototypes. `root` is injected into host calls that omit params.root. `timeout_ms` caps JS execution and subprocess-backed host calls. In Code Mode, analyze, checkArchitecture, securityCandidates, findDupes, impactClosure, checkHealth, audit, impact, checkRuntimeCoverage, getHotPaths, getBlastRadius, getImportance, and getCleanupCandidates stay subprocess-backed and are killed on timeout. Every other host call runs in this process, where `timeout_ms` both answers you on time and sets that call's cancellation token: the analysis is asked to stop rather than only abandoned. The stop is cooperative and has no upper bound, because a token set inside a long analysis stage is not read until that stage ends, so the work may still be winding down after the call returns, and while it is the next in-process call falls back to the killable subprocess. `max_output_bytes` caps the total fallow JSON read by host calls and, separately, the serialized snippet result: a larger result is refused with `ok:false`, `truncated:true`, `result_bytes`, and a short `result_preview` in place of the value, so return a projection rather than a whole report; an oversized thrown error message is clamped too, at `max_output_bytes` or 4096 bytes, whichever is larger, and reported with `truncated:true` and `error_bytes`. Host calls refused before dispatch (unknown tool name, malformed params, an output budget with nothing left) run nothing and do not spend the `max_host_calls` budget; `limits.max_rejected_host_calls` bounds how many of them `calls[]` records. Host calls are memoized for the duration of one snippet: repeating the same tool with the same params (key order does not matter) is served from that snippet's own cache, spends no `max_host_calls` slot and no output budget, and still appears in `calls[]` marked `cache_hit: true`; nothing is cached between invocations. The trace itself is bounded at `limits.max_recorded_calls` entries: beyond that the host calls still run and still return, only their trace entries are dropped, and `calls_omitted` reports how many, so a snippet looping one cached call cannot grow the response without limit. `fallow.all(requests)` fans out independent host calls in one go: `requests` is an array of `{ tool, params }` objects whose `tool` is the same wire name `fallow.run` takes, and the return value is an array positionally aligned with it whose elements are `{ ok: true, value }` or `{ ok: false, error }`, so one failing element never hides the others. Every batch element goes through the same tool validation, `root` injection, memoization, shared deadline, and output-byte accounting as a single call, and each element that actually dispatches spends one `max_host_calls` slot. The output budget is shared rather than per element: what is left of `max_output_bytes` is divided evenly across the dispatches a batch makes, so a fan-out reads at most `max_output_bytes` in total. A batch is refused whole, before anything runs, when an element is not an object carrying a `tool` string, when it holds more than `max_host_calls` elements, or when it needs more dispatches than the budget has left. The snippet stays synchronous, with no promises in the sandbox: `fallow.all` blocks until every element has resolved, overlapping the subprocess-backed elements while in-process ones run one at a time, so a fan-out cannot stack in-process analyses whose only stop is cooperative.

code.description:
JavaScript function expression or function body. The function receives
`{ fallow, root }` and must return a JSON-serializable value.

max_output_bytes.description:
Maximum total bytes of fallow JSON output that sandbox host calls may
read. Defaults to 1000000 and is capped at 4000000.

root.description:
Default project root injected into fallow host calls when their params
omit `root`.

timeout_ms.description:
Overall sandbox timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 5000 and is capped
at 30000.

name: code_execute
